_comment: Scope + allow-list for verify-rule12-freeze.py (the Rule-12 append-only GATE). `enforced_globs` is where an unstamped prose Rule-12 note is a HARD FAIL. Notes outside it are COUNTED and PRINTED as a census on every run, never hidden -- an unenforced surface that is invisible is a hole; one that prints its own size every build is a queue. Every `allow_list` entry MUST carry path + match (a verbatim substring of the note line, so an entry cannot silently widen to a different note) + class + reason; an entry missing any of those FAILS the run, because an allow-list that accepts a bare path is a mute button rather than an exemption. An EMPTY `enforced_globs` also FAILS: a gate that enforces nothing while printing OK is the failure mode this file exists to prevent.
_scope_note: `*.md` -- corpus-wide, every tracked Markdown file. Deliberately not narrowed. Scoping the DETECTOR is exactly how a gate acquires a blind spot: the 2026-08-26 backfill found Rule-12 notes in 267 files across manuscript/ave-kb/ (121), research/ (119), _orchestration/ (27), so any narrower scope would have left a majority of the corpus's frozen bodies unguarded while the gate still printed OK. CURRENT STATE, measured by running the gate rather than asserted (2026-09-06): 428 prose notes recognised, all 428 in enforced scope; 423 served by a stamp; 5 allow-listed -- so the allow_list below carries FIVE entries, in TWO classes. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-06 and the previous figures (455 / 453 / 2, dated 2026-08-27) no longer hold: 30 lines that the detector used to count as notes were not notes at all. 27 of them sat inside a FENCED CODE BLOCK in _orchestration/2026-08-03_link-form-anchor-drift-triage.md -- rows of a fenced tool transcript quoting OTHER files' notes -- and the remaining 3 are table rows in docket entries quoting another file's banner. All 30 stamps were REVERTED (each of those files is now byte-identical to its pre-backfill blob); the 27 are handled structurally by the detector's new fence skip, and the 3 by the `not-a-freeze-note` entries below. An earlier version of this note said 'All 455 notes are stamped; the allow-list carries ONE entry', which contradicted the allow_list in this same file. WHAT 'ALL NOTES SERVED' DOES NOT MEAN. The detector recognises a note only when a Rule-12 marker and a DIRECTIONAL preservation assertion fall on ONE line, OUTSIDE a fenced code block. Notes wrapped across two lines, notes naming no direction, and Rule-12-shaped lines inside fences are outside it by construction; the gate's NON-GATING arms count all THREE families on every run and `--census` lists them. A four-space INDENTED code block is NOT recognised as a fence, so a Rule-12-shaped line inside one is still read as prose -- a named, unclosed blind spot. Separately, the stamps cover less than the span they sit in -- a stamp certifies the longest contiguous unchanged run inside its tile, not the tile -- and the run prints that coverage figure too.

_classes.known-pre-existing-violation: The frozen body has ALREADY drifted. NOT repaired -- repairing it in place would compound the Rule-12 violation by destroying the evidence (flag-don't-fix). The entry carries the diff and the routing.
_classes.not-a-freeze-note: The line matches the detector's phrasing but asserts nothing about bytes in THIS file -- a survey/triage doc quoting another record's note, or a convention doc describing the rule.
_classes.direction-not-determinable: The note names no direction at all, so `region` has no defensible value. (A note naming BOTH is not this class -- it gets two stamps.) Needs the record's author, not a guess.
_classes.generated-artifact: The file is generated, so a stamp would be rewritten by its generator.
_classes.byte-pinned-by-another-gate: Another gate keys on this file's BYTES -- a pinned blob hash, or an adjudication registry keyed on a line's stripped content. Writing a stamp into it breaks that gate, and re-keying someone else's gate so this one can pass is exactly the move this program forbids. The note goes unstamped, deliberately and on the record, with the consequence stated and a routed instruction for when the other pin retires.

allow_list.reason: research/drivers/approach_leak_v2.py READ_ONLY_ARTIFACTS byte-pins this file: its NC-BYTES gate compares `git hash-object` on the live file against a pinned blob, under the frozen purpose 'this lane wrote none of the ten read-only predecessor artifacts'. The 2026-08-26 backfill DID write a stamp here (region=above offset=0 lines=587 bytes=41917 base=f3607be8), and `approach_leak_v2_number_check.py` went RED on it -- caught by running all 34 lane checkers, not by review. The stamp was REVERTED, not the pin: re-pinning another lane's frozen gate so that this gate can pass is the move this program forbids, and the file's own Rule-12 note is exactly the kind of record a byte-pin is meant to protect. CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: the 587-line body above that note is guarded by the v2 lane's blob pin instead of by this gate. That pin is STRICTER (whole-file) but it is not a Rule-12 gate -- it fires for any reason at all, and it will be retired when that lane is. ROUTED: when approach-leak v2's NC-BYTES pin is retired, drop this entry and run `verify-rule12-freeze.py --backfill --path research/2026-08-05_approach-leak_result.md`.

The 2026-08-26 backfill appended a freeze stamp to it (region=below offset=0 lines=149 base=c9d71adc), which changed the line's bytes, un-keyed the existing adjudication, and made the R40 forward guard re-flag it -- caught by the pre-commit `make verify`, not by review. The STAMP was reverted, not the registry: adding this line's new byte-form to another lane's adjudication registry would silently orphan the entry they authored, and their check is not wrong -- my stamp is what moved. CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: the 149 lines below this note are NOT guarded by this gate. ROUTED to the orchestrator, because the clean fix is one line in someone else's file and is theirs to make: teach the R40 guard's content key to strip freeze stamps, exactly as `kb_index_lib._normalize_text` now does -- a machine annotation that renders invisibly must be invisible to content-keyed tooling too. Then drop this entry and run `verify-rule12-freeze.py --backfill --path manuscript/ave-kb/common/port-register.md`.

This line is a cell in this docket entry's inventory table; the preservation words inside it belong to a \noindent\textbf{} banner in a manuscript .tex file, reproduced verbatim as evidence. It asserts nothing whatever about bytes in the docket entry it sits in. The 2026-08-26 backfill nevertheless read it as this file's own freeze note and stamped it region=above lines=142 bytes=9321 base=abb8cd36 -- 142 lines of a docket entry frozen because a table cell quotes somebody else's banner. That stamp certified a span nobody had frozen, and a stamp that certifies an unclaimed span is worse than none: it reads as a guard. REVERTED 2026-09-06; the line is byte-identical to the pre-backfill blob again. ROUTED: if this entry ever wants a real freeze note, it needs one written in its own voice, in prose, outside the table.

The file IS on origin/main and the backfill did see it -- what is unmerged is the Rule-12 NOTE appended to it on branch research/2026-08-26-hb-lens-audit-result (commit 352f16a1). On main the record carries no Rule-12 note at all, which is why it has no stamp and why the gate is correctly silent about it. Verified 2026-08-27: `git ls-tree origin/main` lists the path; `git show origin/main:<path>` matches no Rule-12 marker; the branch copy carries note lines at :180 and :204. NOTE ON :180 SPECIFICALLY -- it reads 'Additive only (Rule 12). Nothing above this line is edited; the body of this' and the DETECTOR WILL NOT RECOGNISE IT: 'is edited' is not a preservation verb, so no directional assertion matches. It is a live instance of the blind-spot family the gate's second arm reports. Stamping it on landing therefore needs the note reworded by its author, or an allow-list entry -- `--backfill --path <path>` alone will not do it.
